A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same regularized personalization method, despite the changed title. All 22 pages of v1 and 25 pages of v3, including their appendices, support comparison; equations, tables and figures are readable.

before.justification: V1 reports original toy diffusion experiments, quantitative and qualitative personalization results, and distribution-preservation and regularization analyses.

after.justification: V3 retains original personalization and toy results and adds experiments across diffusion backbones, training-time measurements, a Lipschitz-constant estimate and a user preference study.

M1.justification: The procedure remains denoising-loss minimization plus a penalty on deviation from pretrained weights. V1 already explicitly implements the squared L2 penalty and omits prior-sample generation. V3 makes these choices clearer in Algorithm 1 and evaluates the same objective with additional backbones and personalization configurations.

E1.justification: The 30-subject DreamBooth benchmark and Gaussian toy task remain. However, v3 removes evaluation on all 1,000 ImageNet class prompts and cat generation after personalization to non-cat subjects, substantially reducing coverage of preservation beyond the personalized subject. The additional diffusion backbones change model configurations rather than dataset coverage.

E2.justification: The eight named personalization baselines remain in Table 2. However, the unpersonalized Pretrained comparator is removed from the corresponding Tables 2 and 4, together with the Real Images reference rows. The new backbone and user comparisons reuse existing baseline methods.

E3.justification: V3 adds SD-XL and SD-3.0 configurations with different optimization budgets, timing comparisons, and a randomized preference protocol covering 30 questions with 35 general-preference raters and 15 detailed-criteria raters. Table 2 adds a joint ranking without specifying its aggregation rule. The toy experiment's reported regularization weight changes from 1 to 50, and one toy sweep setting changes from 100 to 10.

E4.justification: V3 removes the ImageNet IS/FID preservation analysis and non-cat-to-cat test. It adds Jacobian-based Lipschitz estimation, timing analysis, additional regularization examples and failure analyses across backbones. The parameter/output-deviation plot, trade-off curves and learning-rate-matched DreamBooth control are retained, although relocated or combined.

E5.justification: V3 newly reports averaging ten timing trials per backbone–method combination and explicitly fixing training as well as evaluation seeds. V1's IS values with ± terms disappear with the removed experiment. Main DINO/CLIP results remain point estimates, and the new preference study reports percentages without confidence intervals.

E6.justification: V3 adds backbone results, timing results, a Lipschitz estimate of approximately 184, and user preferences of 45.81% for Ours versus 25.14% for DreamBooth. In corresponding Table 2 entries, Custom Diffusion's DINO changes from 0.3126 to 0.5568 and CLIP-T from 0.3179 to 0.3154; Textual Inversion's CLIP-I changes from 0.7608 to 0.7539. Ours remains 0.6394/0.2976/0.7948. ImageNet results are removed, and several qualitative outputs are replaced.

T1.justification: The two theorems and their principal proofs are retained. V3 adds compact-domain attention considerations and a positive noise-floor condition supporting finite constants. New Remark 3 attempts to connect the norm bound to a squared L2 bound; its stated inequality is not justified uniformly as parameter distances approach zero.

C1.justification: The objective-misalignment and bounded-drift claims remain, but v3 expands the main contribution to demonstrated effectiveness across multiple backbones and personalization strategies. It also makes computational efficiency a central claim, explicitly asserting more than a twofold training-time reduction, which v1 did not claim.

C2.justification: New Appendix A distinguishes the theoretical Lipschitz constant from the empirically tuned regularization coefficient and discusses subject-dependent tuning. Expanded limitations explain obstacles to Fisher-weighted regularization without pretraining data. Appendix L interprets backbone-specific identity and prompt failures, including CLIP-T decreases. V1's interpretations of ImageNet distribution proximity are removed.

D1.justification: Appendix H adds backbone-specific learning rates, regularization weights, iteration counts, token choices and implementation information, including the authors' SD-3.0 Custom Diffusion implementation. Appendix D promises code release. Conversely, v1's explicit AdamW optimizer, 50 denoising steps, guidance scale 7.5 and special-token exclusion for CLIP-T are no longer specified. These omissions do not establish actual setting changes.

R1.justification: The central positioning against architectural constraints and resource-intensive distribution matching remains. Section 2 adds image- and text-level prior-preservation work, including FaceChain-SuDe and ClassDiffusion; other additions support attention regularity, SD-3.0 and transfer regularization. Several earlier contextual and removed-evaluation citations disappear. V3 also explicitly acknowledges the conventional L2 form.

P1.justification: V3 substantially rewrites the abstract, introduction and experimental narrative, changes the title, reorganizes experimental subsections and extensively reorders the appendices. It adds separate regularization, reproducibility and LLM-usage discussions and adopts conference-paper headings and front matter.

P2.justification: V3 redraws the toy overview with an ideal-case panel, replaces the method-overview table with a backbone-results table, and adds timing and user-study displays. Table 2 gains grouped categories and rankings. Earlier deviation and trade-off plots are combined into Figure 6; ImageNet and cat figures disappear, while several qualitative panels are revised or added.

improvement.justification: V3 strengthens practical validation through multiple backbones, repeated timing measurements and a randomized user study addressing v1's reliance on automatic metrics. However, it removes the 1,000-class IS/FID evidence supporting the central preservation claim. New material also introduces unresolved problems: the claim of improvements without reductions conflicts with Table 1's CLIP-T decreases, and Remark 3 does not establish its squared-norm bound. These substantive gains and losses leave the net change in overall quality uncertain.
